summary: Four experiments completed in 8.8 minutes, and two were compute-bound. The 8.75-minute Three-family operational-obligation saturation corpus was the measured critical path; the locked indicator records no GPU-idle condition on compute-bound tasks.
bottlenecks_identified: Three-family operational-obligation saturation corpus formed the measured critical path at 8.75 minutes, but the supplied timing has no phase attribution and therefore does not explain why it took longest.
Disk-mtime reconstruction does not correlate task phases with accelerator samples, so end-to-end GPU efficiency cannot be resolved from the monitor snapshot.
Loaded-model concurrency and runner identity were not recorded, leaving DualGPURunner eligibility unobservable.
improvements_suggested: Batch 8-16 compatible questions per forward pass when one model serves multiple prompts.
Record monotonic task-phase timings and task-correlated GPU samples for each compute-bound experiment.
Emit a launch receipt containing loaded-model count, runner identity, and device placement; place an independent concurrent model workload on the unused device only when one is ready.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add monotonic phase clocks and task-correlated GPU samples to compute-bound execution.
Add configurable 8-16 question batching to the single-model inference path.
Record model concurrency and runner selection, then schedule independent concurrent model work across available devices when eligible.
meta_reflection: No data available this milestone attributes the longest task to a specific phase or establishes that any compute-bound task loaded two or more models in parallel. A missed DualGPURunner engagement therefore cannot be identified, and the 0% savings estimate reflects the absence of a timed alternative attributable to the milestone window.
